---
title: "Low-level models and other input styles"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(rxode2)
```

Most of the `rxode2` documentation writes models as model functions,
with an `ini({})` block for the parameter values and a `model({})`
block for the equations, and builds dosing with `et()`.  `rxode2` also
supports other styles, mostly kept from earlier versions and from
other tools.  This page collects them and shows how they behave
differently.

## Low-level models

### Writing a low-level model

A low-level model gives `rxode2()` the model equations only, without
`ini({})`.  It can be written as a block of statements:

```{r low-level-block}
mod <- rxode2({
  ka <- exp(tka)
  cl <- exp(tcl)
  v <- exp(tv)
  d/dt(depot) <- -ka * depot
  d/dt(center) <- ka * depot - cl / v * center
  cp <- center / v
})
mod
```

as a character string:

```{r low-level-string}
modStr <- rxode2("
  d/dt(center) <- -cl / v * center
  cp <- center / v
")
```

or as a file:

```{r low-level-file}
modFile <- tempfile(fileext = ".rxode2")
writeLines(c("d/dt(center) <- -cl / v * center",
             "cp <- center / v"), modFile)
modFile <- rxode2(filename = modFile)
modFile
```

Each call translates the model to C, compiles it and returns an
`rxode2` object.

### Solving: `params=` and `inits=`

A low-level model has no parameter values, so every parameter must be
supplied when solving, with `params=` (a named vector, or a data frame
with one row per subject):

```{r low-level-solve}
ev <- et(amt = 300) |> et(seq(0, 24, by = 2))
s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, params = c(tka = 0.45, tcl = 1, tv = 3.45))
head(s)
```

A missing parameter is an error:

```{r low-level-missing}
try(rxSolve(mod, ev))
```

The state values at time 0 can be given with `inits=` (or with
`state(0) <-` in the model, as in a model function):

```{r low-level-inits}
s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, params = c(tka = 0.45, tcl = 1, tv = 3.45),
             inits = c(depot = 10))
head(s)
```

### How they differ from model functions

The same model as a model function:

```{r fun-form}
modFun <- function() {
  ini({
    tka <- 0.45
    tcl <- 1
    tv <- 3.45
    eta.cl ~ 0.1
    add.sd <- 0.7
  })
  model({
    ka <- exp(tka)
    cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl)
    v <- exp(tv)
    d/dt(depot) <- -ka * depot
    d/dt(center) <- ka * depot - cl / v * center
    cp <- center / v
    cp ~ add(add.sd)
  })
}
ui <- modFun()
```

- **Parameter values.** A model function takes its parameter values
  from `ini({})`, so it solves with `rxSolve(ui, ev)`.  `params=` still
  works and overrides the `ini({})` values.  A low-level model only
  has the values supplied with `params=`.

- **Between-subject variability.** The `eta.cl ~ 0.1` line in
  `ini({})` is used to simulate the etas.  A low-level model has no
  omega; it has to be given with `omega=` in `rxSolve()`.

- **Residual error.** `cp ~ add(add.sd)` defines an endpoint with
  residual error; solving simulates it in the `sim` column (`ipredSim`
  is the prediction).  The low-level language does not have endpoints:
  there `~` is an assignment that is not included in the output, and
  residual error terms have to be written by hand with `sigma=` in
  `rxSolve()`.

```{r fun-solve}
rxSolve(ui, ev, seed = 42)
```

```{r low-level-tilde}
hidden <- rxode2({
  a ~ 3
  b <- a + 1
})
hidden$lhs # `a` is not output
```

```{r low-level-no-endpoint}
try(rxode2({
  cp <- center / v
  cp ~ add(add.sd)
}))
```

- **Turning the variability off.** For a model function, `omega = NA`
  and `sigma = NA` give the typical-value prediction (in the `pred`
  column):

```{r fun-typical}
rxSolve(ui, ev, params = c(tcl = 2), omega = NA, sigma = NA)
```

- **Model piping.** `model()` and `ini()` piping work on the model
  function form.  Piping a low-level model first converts it to a
  model function:

```{r low-level-pipe}
mod |> ini(tka = 0.45, tcl = 1, tv = 3.45)
```

### Converting between forms

- `ui$simulationModel` (or `ui$simulationIniModel`, which also includes
  the `ini({})` values) gives the low-level model that `rxode2` solves
  for a model function, including the generated code for the endpoints:

```{r sim-model}
ui$simulationModel
```

- `as.rxUi()` converts a low-level model to a model function object
  (`rxUi`); it has no `ini({})` values:

```{r as-rxui}
modUi <- as.rxUi(mod)
modUi$iniDf
```

- `as.function()` (or `$fun`) gives back the model function itself:

```{r as-function}
as.function(modUi)
```

### When a low-level model is still the right tool

- **Models in packages.** `rxPkg()` and `rxUse()` store compiled
  low-level models in a package (see
  [Pre-compiled models in packages](https://nlmixr2.github.io/rxode2/articles/rxode2-rxUse.html)).
- **Generated code.** When a tool writes the model text, the string
  and file forms take it directly.
- **Options of the compiled model.** Options such as `calcJac=` (a
  symbolic Jacobian, see
  [stiff ODEs](https://nlmixr2.github.io/rxode2/articles/rxode2-stiff.html))
  are arguments of `rxode2()`.
- **All parameters per subject.** When every parameter comes from a
  data frame with `params=`, an `ini({})` block adds nothing.
- **C-level functions.** Packages that provide C functions to
  `rxode2` models
  ([custom C/C++ functions](rxode2-pkg-exported-funs.html)) document
  the low-level form.

## Other event-table styles

The main way to build dosing and sampling is `et()` (see
[event tables](https://nlmixr2.github.io/rxode2/articles/rxode2-event-table.html)).
`rxSolve()` also accepts the styles below.

### `eventTable()` methods

The classic `RxODE` interface creates an event table and then calls
methods on it:

```{r event-table}
evt <- eventTable(amount.units = "mg", time.units = "hours")
evt$add.dosing(dose = 300, nbr.doses = 3, dosing.interval = 12)
evt$add.sampling(seq(0, 36, by = 4))
evt
```

The same methods are functions that can be piped:

```{r event-table-pipe}
evt2 <- eventTable() |>
  add.dosing(dose = 300, nbr.doses = 3, dosing.interval = 12) |>
  add.sampling(seq(0, 36, by = 4))
rxSolve(ui, evt2, omega = NA, sigma = NA)
```

### NONMEM-style data frames

A data frame with NONMEM columns (`ID`, `TIME`, `AMT`, `EVID`, `CMT`,
`RATE`, `II`, `ADDL`, `SS`, `DV`, ...) is used directly (see
[dataset columns](https://nlmixr2.github.io/rxode2/articles/rxode2-dataset-columns.html)):

```{r nonmem-df}
nmData <- data.frame(ID = 1,
                     TIME = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12),
                     AMT = c(300, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
                     EVID = c(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
                     CMT = 1)
rxSolve(ui, nmData, omega = NA, sigma = NA)
```

### deSolve-style event data frames

A `deSolve` event data frame (columns `var`, `time`, `value` and
`method`, with `method` one of `"add"`, `"mult"` or `"rep"`) is
converted by `et()` to dose (`evid=1`), multiply (`evid=6`) and replace
(`evid=5`) events:

```{r desolve-df}
eventdat <- data.frame(var = c("depot", "center", "center"),
                       time = c(0, 6, 12),
                       value = c(300, 2, 0),
                       method = c("add", "mult", "rep"))
ev3 <- et(eventdat) |> et(seq(0, 24, by = 2))
rxSolve(ui, ev3, omega = NA, sigma = NA)
```

### Classic RxODE `evid` codes

`rxode2` also accepts the classic `RxODE` event ids, which combine the
compartment, the dose type and the infusion flags in one number.  They
are described in
[classic RxODE events](https://nlmixr2.github.io/rxode2/articles/rxode2-events-classic.html).
